label: Profile Card
title: Profile Card
summary: Use a Profile Card to show who the user is on a dark panel: initials or a photo, a name, UPI handles, and account rows below.
corePrinciple: Who you are, and the handles you share.

configuration.title: A header, a body, and a gold option
configuration.description: name, monogram, and upiHandles make the header. avatarSource shows a photo in place of the initials, badgeIcon={null} removes the QR badge, and upiHandles={[]} leaves just the name. children is the body, under a divider; leave it out for a header-only card. header replaces the avatar, name, and handles together. Profile Card Appearance Premium turns the panel gold. The card passes its on-dark modes to everything inside, so ListItem titles, icons, chevrons, and Buttons turn white or gold on their own; plain Text and support text don’t.

states.title: Handles you can press
states.description: The card itself isn’t pressable. A handle with onPress is a button that shrinks a little while pressed, usually to copy it; one without is plain text. Body rows keep their own states, such as a ListItem with onPress. There’s no selected, disabled, or loading state.

sizing.title: 344 px, or the host’s width
sizing.description: The card is 344 px wide, as Figma draws it; width takes another number, or a percentage such as '100%' to fill its host. Height follows the content: 20 px of padding, and 12 px between the header, the divider, and each body row. A long name ends in …, and the handles wrap onto another line.

content.title: A name, initials, and handles as people type them
content.description: name is the person’s display name, and monogram their two initials. A handle’s label is the UPI ID or the phone number exactly as people would type it: use ic_copy on a handle people copy and ic_confirm on a verified number. Keep body rows to short titles, with one Button or a chevron each.

inContext.title: The Profile screen
inContext.description: The card heads the Profile screen. Copying a handle and opening a row are the screen’s own work, through each handle’s and row’s onPress; the card only lays them out.

sources.title: Use the public Profile Card contract
sources.description: The guide compares the Figma component with the installed package and its Storybook stories.
blocks: Installed jfs-components is 0.1.78 (19 October build of Biscuit’s main) from the team’s private package repository. Figma’s Profile Card has one property, the body slot; the name, handles, badge, and photo are overrides there, and Premium is a variable mode. The card gives its children on-dark modes, but plain Text and ListItem support text stay dark on the navy panel, as in Figma’s own sample, and a child’s own modes override the card’s. The header is 48 px tall where Figma’s is 47, and the QR glyph is near-black, not grey. List Item Style Boxed covers the card in white boxes, and a long handle never ends in …, so its UPI Handle runs past the card. The published Storybook is older than the installed package and still shows the older generated page (all reported).
